1.1: This how the story start—the good news bout Jesus Christ, God's Son.
1.2: Just like the prophets said: "I'm sendin' My messenger ahead of You, he gon' clear the way."
1.3: A voice cryin' out in the wild sayin': "Get ready for the Lord to come through. Straighten out His path."
1.4: So John showed up in the wild, dunkin' folks in the Jordan River, tellin' 'em to repent so they could get their sins wiped clean.
1.5: Everybody from Judea and Jerusalem came through, confessin' their mess and gettin' baptized.
1.6: John was rockin' camel hair with a leather belt, and his meals? Locusts and wild honey.
1.7: He was preachin', sayin', "Somebody stronger than me comin' up after this. I ain't even worthy to lace His sandals.
1.8: I baptize y'all with water, but He gon' baptize y'all with the Holy Ghost."
1.9: Around that time, Jesus came from Nazareth up in Galilee, and John baptized Him in the Jordan.
1.10: Soon as Jesus came up out that water, the sky cracked open and the Spirit came down like a dove.
1.11: Then a voice from heaven said, "You My Son. I love You. I'm proud of You."
1.12: Right after that, the Spirit led Jesus into the wilderness.
1.13: He stayed out there forty days, gettin' tested by Satan. He was chillin' with wild animals, and angels came through to look after Him.
1.14: After John got locked up, Jesus hit Galilee preachin' the gospel from God.
1.15: He said, "The time is now. God's Kingdom pullin' up. Turn from your old ways and believe this good news."
1.16: Jesus was walkin' by the Sea of Galilee and saw Simon and Andrew tossin' nets—they was fishin'.
1.17: He told 'em, "Come roll with Me, and I'll show y'all how to fish for people."
1.18: They dropped their nets with the quickness and followed Him.
1.19: A little further down, He saw James and John (Zebedee's sons) in the boat fixin' nets.
1.20: He called them too, and they left their daddy and the workers right there and followed Jesus.
1.21: They all rolled into Capernaum, and on the Sabbath, Jesus hit the synagogue and started teachin'.
1.22: Folks were shook by how He taught—like He really knew what He was talkin' about, not like the regular religious teachers.
1.23: Then this man with a dirty spirit popped off right there,
1.24: sayin', "What you want with us, Jesus of Nazareth? You here to destroy us? I know who You are—God's Holy One!"
1.25: Jesus checked that spirit quick: "Shut up and get outta him."
1.26: The demon made the man spazz out and screamed loud, then bounced.
1.27: Everybody was wildin' like, "Yo! Who is this dude? Even demons listen to Him?"
1.28: Word spread all over Galilee fast.
1.29: Soon as they left the synagogue, they went to Simon and Andrew's crib, with James and John.
1.30: Simon's mother-in-law had a fever, and they told Jesus.
1.31: He grabbed her hand, helped her up—and boom, fever gone. She got up and started serving.
1.32: That night, after sunset, folks brought everybody sick and demon-possessed to Jesus.
1.33: The whole city was posted at the door.
1.34: Jesus healed all kinds of diseases and cast out a bunch of demons. He wouldn't let 'em talk though—they already knew who He was.
1.35: Before the sun came up, Jesus dipped to a quiet spot and prayed.
1.36: Simon and the crew went lookin' for Him.
1.37: When they found Him, they said, "Everybody lookin' for You!"
1.38: Jesus said, "Let's hit up the next towns. That's why I came—to preach everywhere."
1.39: And that's what He did—preachin' in synagogues and castin' out demons across Galilee.
1.40: A man with leprosy came beggin' Jesus on his knees, "If You want to, You can heal me."
1.41: Jesus felt that. He touched him and said, "I want to. Be healed."
1.42: Right then, the leprosy bounced. The man was clean.
1.43: Jesus told him sternly, "Don't tell nobody.
1.44: Go show the priest and make the offering Moses talked about as proof you clean."
1.45: But the man was too hyped—he ran and told everybody. Because of that, Jesus couldn't move around openly. He stayed out in quiet spots, but people still pulled up from all over.

2.1: A few days later, Jesus pulled up in Capernaum again, and folks found out He was in the house.
2.2: People came runnin'—so many that the place was packed, even outside the door. Jesus was in there preachin' the word.
2.3: Then these four dudes came through carryin' they paralyzed homeboy on a mat.
2.4: They couldn't get through the crowd, so they climbed up, tore open the roof, and lowered him down right in front of Jesus.
2.5: Jesus peeped their faith and said to the man, "Son, your sins forgiven."
2.6: Some of the teachers of the law was sittin' there, thinkin' to themselves,
2.7: "Who this man think He is? Only God can forgive sins."
2.8: Jesus, knowin' what they was thinkin' deep down, said, "Why y'all trippin' in your hearts?
2.9: What's easier—to say 'your sins are forgiven' or 'get up and walk'?
2.10: But just so y'all know the Son of Man got authority down here to forgive sin…" He turned to the man and said,
2.11: "Get up, take your mat, and go home."
2.12: And just like that, dude stood up, grabbed his mat, and walked out in front of everybody. Folks was stunned—like "We ain't never seen nothin' like this!"
2.13: Jesus went back out by the water, and crowds gathered again. He kept teachin'.
2.14: He saw Levi (also known as Matthew), chillin' at the tax booth. Jesus said, "Follow Me," and Levi got up and followed.
2.15: Later on, Jesus was eatin' dinner at Levi's house. A bunch of tax collectors and folks labeled "sinners" was there too. They liked rollin' with Jesus.
2.16: But when the religious folks saw Him eatin' with them, they asked the disciples, "Why He hangin' with folks like that?"
2.17: Jesus heard and clapped back: "Healthy folks don't need a doctor—sick folks do. I didn't come for the so-called righteous, but for the ones who know they need help."
2.18: Some folks came up—John's disciples and the Pharisees' crew—and said, "Why your disciples ain't fasting like we do?"
2.19: Jesus told 'em, "You don't fast at a wedding while the groom's still there, right? Nah, you celebrate.
2.20: But once the groom gone, then yeah—they'll fast."
2.21: "Look—nobody patches old clothes with brand new cloth, or the rip just gets worse.
2.22: Same with wine—new wine don't go in old wineskins. It'll bust 'em wide open. New wine gotta go in fresh skins."
2.23: One Sabbath day, Jesus and His boys was walkin' through some grainfields. They started pickin' off grain as they walked.
2.24: Pharisees popped off like, "Yo! Why they breakin' Sabbath law?"
2.25: Jesus hit 'em with a throwback: "Y'all forgot what David did when he and his people was hungry?
2.26: He went in God's house, took the holy bread—meant only for priests—and fed his crew."
2.27: Then He dropped the mic: "The Sabbath was made for man, not the other way around.
2.28: So yeah—the Son of Man is Lord, even of the Sabbath."

3.1: Jesus slid back into the synagogue, and there was a man in there with a messed-up hand.
3.2: The haters was watchin' Him close, tryna catch Him slippin' if He healed on the Sabbath, so they could come for Him.
3.3: Jesus looked at the man and said, "Come stand up here in front of everybody."
3.4: Then He looked at the crowd and asked, "Y'all tell me—is it right to do good or evil on the Sabbath? Save a life or let somebody die?" But they ain't say nothin'.
3.5: Jesus looked around, mad and hurt at how cold-hearted they were. Then He told the man, "Stretch your hand out." And when the man did, his hand was fully healed—just like the other one.
3.6: The Pharisees dipped out and linked up with the Herodians right then, plottin' on how to take Jesus out.
3.7: Jesus and His crew headed out toward the lake, and a crowd followed—folks from Galilee, Judea,
3.8: Jerusalem, Idumea, the east side of the Jordan, even Tyre and Sidon. Word had spread about what He was doin', so they all pulled up.
3.9: Jesus told His disciples to keep a boat nearby, just in case the crowd got too wild and pressed in on Him.
3.10: He had healed so many folks that everybody with somethin' wrong was tryna touch Him.
3.11: Even unclean spirits would fall out when they saw Him, yellin', "You the Son of God!"
3.12: But Jesus would shut 'em down quick, tellin' them not to say who He was.
3.13: Jesus went up the mountain and called the ones He wanted. They came.
3.14: He chose twelve of them to roll with Him and to be sent out to preach,
3.15: and to have power to heal and cast out demons.
3.16: He picked Simon and called him Peter,
3.17: James and John (Zebedee's sons), and He nicknamed them Boanerges, which means "Sons of Thunder."
3.18: Then Andrew, Philip, Bartholomew, Matthew, Thomas, James (son of Alphaeus), Thaddaeus, Simon the Zealot,
3.19: and Judas Iscariot—the same one who ended up betrayin' Him. Then they went inside a house.
3.20: The crowd came back together, deep again, to the point Jesus and them couldn't even eat.
3.21: When His family heard what was goin' on, they tried to go get Him, sayin', "He done lost His mind."
3.22: Some scribes came down from Jerusalem and said, "He got Beelzebub in Him. That's how He castin' out demons—by the prince of demons."
3.23: Jesus called them over and told 'em stories: "How Satan gon' cast out Satan?
3.24: If a kingdom beefin' with itself, it ain't gon' last.
3.25: Same thing with a house divided—it falls apart.
3.26: So if Satan is fightin' himself, he already done.
3.27: Nobody breaks into a strong man's house and takes his stuff unless he ties that man up first. Then he can rob him clean."
3.28: "Listen close—every sin, every wild word people say, can be forgiven.
3.29: But if you disrespect the Holy Spirit? That's different. That's a forever sin. No forgiveness for that—just judgment."
3.30: He said that 'cause they kept sayin' He had an unclean spirit.
3.31: Then Jesus' mama and brothers showed up, standin' outside, callin' for Him.
3.32: The crowd told Him, "Hey, your family outside askin' for you."
3.33: But Jesus said, "Who y'all think my real family is?"
3.34: He looked around at the folks sittin' with Him and said, "Here go my real family."
3.35: "Anybody doin' God's will? That's my brother, my sister, and my mama."

4.1: Jesus started teachin' again by the lake. A huge crowd pulled up, so He got in a boat and sat out on the water, while everybody stood on land listenin'.
4.2: He dropped a lotta wisdom using parables. And this is how He kicked it off:
4.3: "Listen up! A farmer went out to plant some seeds.
4.4: As he threw them out, some landed on the roadside. Birds came through quick and ate it up.
4.5: Some hit rocky ground, where there wasn't much dirt. They popped up fast, since the soil wasn't deep.
4.6: But the sun came out, and since they ain't have no roots, they dried up quick.
4.7: Other seeds landed where thorns were growin'. The thorns choked 'em out—no harvest.
4.8: But some landed on good soil. Those seeds grew, multiplied, and brought back thirty, sixty, even a hundred times more than what was planted."
4.9: Then He said, "If you got ears, listen close."
4.10: Later on, when it was just Him and the Twelve, they asked about the parables.
4.11: He told them, "Y'all been given the inside scoop on the Kingdom of God. But to everybody else, I gotta speak in code.
4.12: So that, 'They see it, but they don't get it, They hear it, but it don't click— Otherwise, they'd turn around, And get forgiven.'"
4.13: Then He said, "Y'all don't understand this one? How you gon' catch the rest?
4.14: The farmer is plantin' the word.
4.15: The ones on the path? That's folks who hear it, but Satan snatch it before it sinks in.
4.16: The rocky ground? That's folks who get hype real fast,
4.17: but they shallow. Soon as life gets hard or people come for them over the word, they fall off.
4.18: The ones planted in the thorns? They hear it too,
4.19: but life stress, money lies, and all that shiny stuff choke it out—no fruit, no change.
4.20: But the good soil? That's folks who hear the word, hold on to it, and let it grow—some see 30x, 60x, or 100x returns."
4.21: He said, "You don't light a lamp and hide it under the bed, right? Nah, you put it up where it shine.
4.22: 'Cause whatever's in the dark gon' come to light.
4.23: If you got ears, then use 'em."
4.24: Then He added, "Pay attention to what you listen to. However you measure others, that same energy comin' back to you—with interest.
4.25: Whoever got somethin' gon' get even more. But the one slackin'? Even that little bit gon' be snatched."
4.26: He said, "The Kingdom of God is like this: A man plants seeds, goes to sleep, wakes up—day in, day out—
4.27: and the seeds grow on their own. He don't even know how.
4.28: The earth just does what it do: first the blade, then the head, then the full grain.
4.29: And when the crop ready, he grabs the sickle—it's harvest time."
4.30: Then He asked, "What can we compare the Kingdom to? How we gon' paint this picture?
4.31: It's like a mustard seed. Smallest thing you ever seen when it's planted,
4.32: but when it grow? It turn into the biggest plant out there—branches so big even birds chill in its shade."
4.33: Jesus kept teachin' like this, droppin' parables that the crowd could handle.
4.34: He ain't teach without a parable. But when He got His crew alone, He broke it all down.
4.35: That same day, when night hit, He told them, "Let's head across to the other side."
4.36: They left the crowd, and the disciples took Him just like He was in the boat. A few other boats followed too.
4.37: Then outta nowhere, a huge storm hit—waves slammin' into the boat. Water was floodin' in.
4.38: Meanwhile, Jesus was chillin' in the back, sleep on a pillow. They woke Him up like, "Teacher! You don't care we about to drown?"
4.39: He stood up, told the wind, "Chill out!" and told the waves, "Be still!" Everything got quiet. Calm like never before.
4.40: Then He looked at them and said, "Why y'all so shook? Where's your faith?"
4.41: They were shook for real now. Whisperin' to each other, "Who is this man? Even the wind and the waves do what He say!"

5.1: Jesus and them pulled up on the other side of the lake, in the area of the Gadarenes.
5.2: Soon as He stepped out the boat, this man with an unclean spirit came runnin' from the graveyard to meet Him.
5.3: Dude was livin' out there in the tombs. Nobody could hold him down—not even with chains.
5.4: They tried shackles and chains before, but he kept snappin' out of 'em like it was nothin'. Nobody could calm him down.
5.5: All day and night, he'd be out in the hills or in the tombs, screamin' and cuttin' himself with stones.
5.6: When he saw Jesus from a distance, he ran up and bowed down before Him.
5.7: He shouted real loud, "What do You want with me, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? I beg You, don't torture me!"
5.8: (That's 'cause Jesus had already said, "Come outta that man, unclean spirit!")
5.9: Then Jesus asked, "What's your name?" The spirit answered, "My name is Legion, 'cause we deep."
5.10: And the demons begged Jesus not to send them out the area.
5.11: There was a huge herd of pigs eatin' nearby on the hillside.
5.12: The demons said, "Let us go into those pigs!"
5.13: Jesus gave the word, and boom—those spirits jumped in the pigs. Around 2,000 pigs ran wild down the hill straight into the lake and drowned.
5.14: The pig herders took off runnin' and told everybody in town and the countryside. Folks came to see what went down.
5.15: When they got there, they saw the man who used to be possessed sittin' there dressed, calm, and sane. And folks got shook.
5.16: The ones who saw it firsthand told the story about the man and what happened to the pigs.
5.17: Then the people started beggin' Jesus to leave they area.
5.18: As Jesus got in the boat, the man who had been delivered tried to go with Him.
5.19: But Jesus told him, "Nah, go back home to your people. Tell 'em all the good things the Lord did for you, and how He looked out with compassion."
5.20: So the man went through the whole region of Decapolis tellin' everybody what Jesus did for him. Folks were amazed.
5.21: Jesus went back across the lake, and a big crowd gathered by the water.
5.22: One of the synagogue leaders, Jairus, showed up. Soon as he saw Jesus, he dropped to his knees.
5.23: He begged Him, "My daughter's dyin'. Please come lay hands on her so she can live."
5.24: Jesus rolled with him, and the crowd was thick around them.
5.25: A woman who had been dealin' with a nonstop blood flow for twelve years was there too.
5.26: She'd been through it—sufferin' under doctors, spent all her money, and only got worse.
5.27: But when she heard about Jesus, she slid through the crowd and touched His clothes from behind.
5.28: She thought, "If I could just touch His clothes, I know I'll be healed."
5.29: And just like that, the bleeding stopped. She felt it—her body was healed for real.
5.30: Jesus felt the power leave Him and turned around, askin', "Who touched my clothes?"
5.31: The disciples was like, "Bruh, you see this crowd pressin' in, and you askin' who touched you?"
5.32: But He kept lookin' around tryin' to spot who did it.
5.33: The woman stepped up, nervous and shaky, and fell at His feet tellin' the whole truth.
5.34: Jesus told her, "Daughter, your faith healed you. Go in peace, and be free from your suffering."
5.35: While He was still speakin', folks came from Jairus' house sayin', "Your daughter's dead. Don't bother the Teacher anymore."
5.36: But Jesus didn't trip. He looked at Jairus and said, "Don't be scared. Just believe."
5.37: He only let Peter, James, and John roll with Him from there.
5.38: When they got to the house, it was chaos—folks cryin', screamin', carryin' on.
5.39: Jesus walked in like, "Why all the drama? The girl ain't dead, she just sleepin'."
5.40: They laughed at Him. But He made 'em all step outside. Then He took the girl's mom, dad, and the three disciples in the room with Him.
5.41: He grabbed the girl's hand and said, "Talitha, cumi," which means, "Little girl, I'm tellin' you—get up!"
5.42: Instantly, the twelve-year-old girl got up and started walkin' around. Everybody there was shook and amazed.
5.43: Jesus told them, "Keep this on the low," and then said, "Get her somethin' to eat."

6.1: Jesus left that place and went back to His hometown. His disciples rolled with Him.
6.2: When Sabbath came, He started teachin' in the synagogue. Folks heard Him and was shocked like, "Where He get all this from? How He talkin' this wise? And how He doin' all these miracles with His hands?"
6.3: "Ain't this the carpenter? Mary's son? James, Joses, Judas, and Simon's brother? Ain't His sisters right here with us?" They got offended—mad uncomfortable with who He was.
6.4: But Jesus told 'em, "A prophet get respect everywhere except in his own hometown, with his own people, and even in his own house."
6.5: He couldn't do no big miracles there, just laid hands on a few sick folks and healed them.
6.6: He was amazed at how little faith they had. So He kept it movin', goin' around to other villages teachin'.
6.7: Jesus called up the Twelve and sent 'em out two by two. Gave them authority to cast out evil spirits.
6.8: He told 'em, "Don't take nothin' for the road—just a staff. No food, no bag, no coins in your pockets."
6.9: "Wear sandals, but don't pack extra clothes."
6.10: "Wherever y'all stay, stay there 'til you leave that town."
6.11: "If folks don't welcome y'all or listen, shake the dust off your feet when you bounce. That's your sign against them. I'm tellin' you—it'll be easier for Sodom and Gomorrah on judgment day than for that town."
6.12: So they went out preachin', tellin' folks to turn back to God.
6.13: They cast out a bunch of demons, anointed sick people with oil, and healed 'em.
6.14: Word about Jesus got out, and King Herod heard about Him. Herod said, "That must be John the Baptist raised from the dead. That's why He got power like that."
6.15: Some folks was sayin', "Nah, it's Elijah." Others said, "He one of the prophets from back in the day."
6.16: But Herod kept sayin', "Nope, that's John—the one I had beheaded. He back."
6.17: See, Herod had locked John up 'cause of Herodias, his brother Philip's wife—whom he had married.
6.18: John had told Herod, "It ain't right for you to be with your brother's wife."
6.19: Herodias had beef and wanted John dead, but she couldn't pull it off.
6.20: Herod actually respected John. He knew John was righteous and holy. He kept him safe. When he listened to John, he got real conflicted, but he liked hearin' him speak.
6.21: One day on Herod's birthday, he threw a party for his big shots and leaders.
6.22: Herodias's daughter came in and danced. She had everybody—including Herod—impressed. So the king told her, "Ask me anything you want—I got you."
6.23: He even swore, "I'll give you whatever you want, up to half my kingdom."
6.24: She ran to her mama and asked, "What should I ask for?" Her mama said, "The head of John the Baptist."
6.25: The girl rushed back to the king and said, "I want John the Baptist's head—on a platter. Right now."
6.26: Herod felt sick about it. But 'cause of his promise—and everybody watchin'—he ain't wanna go back on his word.
6.27: So he sent the executioner to the prison. Dude chopped off John's head,
6.28: brought it back on a platter, and gave it to the girl. Then she gave it to her mama.
6.29: When John's disciples heard what happened, they came, got his body, and laid it in a tomb.
6.30: The apostles came back to Jesus and told Him everything they'd done and taught.
6.31: He said, "Come on, let's dip to a quiet place and rest." Folks had been runnin' up all day—they ain't even had time to eat.
6.32: So they got in a boat and left for a quiet spot by themselves.
6.33: But people saw them leave and ran from all the towns to meet them. They got there before Jesus and His crew did.
6.34: When Jesus got out the boat, He saw the huge crowd and felt for them—they was like sheep with no shepherd. So He started teachin' them a bunch.
6.35: It was gettin' late. The disciples came up like, "We out in the sticks and it's already late."
6.36: "Send the folks away so they can go buy food in the nearby towns."
6.37: But Jesus said, "Nah, y'all feed them." They said, "You want us to spend 200 silver coins on bread for everybody?"
6.38: Jesus said, "How many loaves y'all got? Go check." They came back sayin', "Five loaves and two fish."
6.39: He told everybody to sit down in groups on the green grass.
6.40: So they sat down in sections—some in hundreds, some in fifties.
6.41: Jesus took the five loaves and two fish, looked up to heaven, blessed the food, broke the loaves, and handed them to the disciples to pass out. He split the fish too, and made sure everybody got some.
6.42: Everybody ate till they was full.
6.43: Then they picked up twelve baskets full of leftovers.
6.45: Right after that, Jesus told His disciples to get in the boat and head to Bethsaida. He stayed back to send the crowd away.
6.46: After the crowd left, He went up a mountain to pray.
6.47: That evening, the boat was in the middle of the lake, and Jesus was still on land.
6.48: He saw them strugglin' to row 'cause the wind was wild. Around 3 a.m., He walked out to them—on the water! He was about to pass them.
6.49: But they saw Him walkin' on the sea and thought He was a ghost. They screamed.
6.50: They all saw Him and was shook. But He said, "Chill out. It's Me. Don't be scared."
6.51: He climbed in the boat, and the wind calmed down. They was shook, mind blown.
6.52: They ain't get the miracle with the loaves—'cause their hearts was still hard.
6.53: When they crossed over, they landed at Gennesaret and docked the boat.
6.54: Soon as they got off, people recognized Jesus.
6.55: Folks ran all through the area, bringing sick people on mats to wherever they heard Jesus was.
6.56: Wherever He went—villages, towns, or countryside—people brought the sick out to the streets. They begged just to touch His cloak. And whoever touched Him? Got healed.

7.1: Some Pharisees and a few scribes pulled up from Jerusalem to check Jesus.
7.2: They saw some of His disciples eating without washing their hands the "right way," and they had a problem with it.
7.3: See, the Pharisees and all the other Jews don't eat unless they wash their hands real specific, followin' what their elders passed down.
7.4: They won't eat after hittin' the market unless they wash up first. They even wash cups, jugs, pots, and couches like it's part of worship.
7.5: So the Pharisees and scribes asked Jesus, "Why Your crew don't follow the elders' traditions? They out here eatin' without even washing up."
7.6: Jesus said, "Isaiah was talkin' about y'all when he called folks hypocrites: 'These people honor Me with their words, but their hearts? They way off.'
7.7: They worship Me for nothin', just teachin' man-made rules like they God's word."
7.8: "Y'all be ditchin' God's commands just to keep your little traditions. Washing pitchers and cups like that's gon' save you."
7.9: "You real slick with it—always tossin' God's law to the side so you can protect your customs."
7.10: "Moses said, 'Honor your mama and daddy,' and, 'If you curse 'em, you dead.'
7.11: But y'all say, 'If a man tells his parents, "What I was gon' do for you is now Corban—a gift to God,"
7.12: then he ain't gotta do nothin' for them.' Like, what?
7.13: You makin' God's Word useless just to hold onto these man-made hand-me-down rules. And this ain't the only thing y'all be doin'."
7.14: Then Jesus turned to the crowd and said, "Y'all listen up and get this:
7.15: Ain't nothin' from outside a person that can make them dirty spiritually. It's what come out they mouth, out they heart—that's the real mess."
7.16: "If you got ears, hear what I'm sayin'."
7.17: When they got inside the house, away from the crowd, the disciples was like, "Umm, so about that parable…"
7.18: Jesus looked at them like, "Y'all don't get it either? Whatever goes in your mouth don't touch your heart—it just hit your stomach and slide out. That ain't what messes you up."
7.19: (And just like that, Jesus made all foods clean.)
7.20: He kept goin': "It's what come outta folks that defiles them.
7.21: From deep inside—out the heart—come evil thoughts, cheating, sex outside God's plan, murder,
7.22: stealing, greed, wickedness, lying, wild living, jealousy, slander, pride, and dumb decisions.
7.23: All that mess come from within, and that's what makes somebody dirty."
7.24: After that, Jesus dipped out to Tyre and Sidon. He tried to keep a low profile, but word got out.
7.25: A woman with a daughter who had a demon in her came through, dropped to His feet.
7.26: She wasn't Jewish—she was Syro-Phoenician. But she was beggin' Jesus to cast the demon out her child.
7.27: Jesus said, "Let the children eat first. It ain't right to take their food and toss it to dogs."
7.28: She fired back, "Yeah, but even the dogs get the crumbs that fall off the kids' table."
7.29: Jesus said, "Whew, sis! That kind of faith? Go 'head. That demon gone."
7.30: She ran back home and found her daughter chillin' on the bed, demon-free.
7.31: Jesus left Tyre and Sidon and went back around to the Sea of Galilee, through the region of Decapolis.
7.32: Some folks brought Him a man who couldn't hear and barely talked. They was beggin' Jesus to lay hands on him.
7.33: Jesus took the man away from the crowd, put His fingers in the guy's ears, then spit and touched his tongue.
7.34: Lookin' up to heaven, Jesus sighed and said, "Ephphatha," which means, "Be opened."
7.35: Instantly the man could hear, and his tongue loosened up. He started speakin' clear.
7.36: Jesus told them not to tell nobody, but they couldn't hold it in. The more He told them, the more they ran tellin' everybody.
7.37: Folks was shook in the best way. "This man do everything right! He makin' the deaf hear and the mute talk!"

8.1: Back in those days, a big crowd had gathered, and folks was hungry. Jesus called His crew together and said,
8.2: "Man, I feel for these people. They been rollin' with Me three whole days and ain't had nothin' to eat.
8.3: If I send 'em home now, stomachs empty, they gon' pass out on the way. Some of 'em came from way out."
8.4: The disciples were like, "How we supposed to feed this many people out here in the middle of nowhere?"
8.5: Jesus said, "How many loaves y'all got?" They said, "Seven."
8.6: So Jesus told the crowd to sit down. He grabbed the bread, gave thanks, broke it up, and gave it to the disciples to pass around.
8.7: They had a few little fish too, so He blessed those and had 'em serve that as well.
8.8: Everybody ate till they were full. Then they picked up seven big baskets of leftovers.
8.9: Around four thousand people got fed. Then Jesus sent them home.
8.10: He and His crew hopped in the boat and headed for Dalmanutha.
8.11: The Pharisees pulled up like haters, tryna test Him. "Show us a sign from heaven!" they said.
8.12: Jesus sighed deep—like real deep—and said, "Why y'all always need a sign? I promise y'all ain't gettin' one."
8.13: Then He left 'em behind and went back across the water.
8.14: Meanwhile, the disciples realized they forgot to bring bread—only had one loaf in the boat.
8.15: Jesus told them, "Look… watch out for the yeast of the Pharisees and Herod."
8.16: They looked at each other like, "See? It's 'cause we ain't bring bread."
8.17: Jesus caught on real quick: "Y'all serious right now? Still don't get it? Heart still hard?
8.18: You got eyes but can't see? Ears but can't hear? Don't y'all remember what just happened?"
8.19: "When I broke the five loaves for the 5,000, how many baskets y'all pick up?" They said, "Twelve."
8.20: "And when I fed the 4,000 with seven loaves?" They said, "Seven baskets."
8.21: "So how y'all still don't get it?"
8.22: They pulled up in Bethsaida. Some folks brought a blind man to Jesus, beggin' for a touch.
8.23: Jesus took the man by the hand and walked him outta town. Then He spit on the man's eyes and laid hands on him. "You see anything?"
8.24: The man looked up and said, "I see people… they look like trees walkin'."
8.25: Jesus laid hands on him again, and this time? He saw everything clearly.
8.26: Jesus said, "Go home. Don't even stop in town or tell nobody."
8.27: Then Jesus and the crew headed to the towns around Caesarea Philippi. On the road He asked, "Who people say I am?"
8.28: They said, "Some say John the Baptist. Others think you Elijah. Some say you just one of the prophets."
8.29: He asked, "But what about y'all? Who do you say I am?" Peter said, "You the Christ."
8.31: Then He started tellin' them straight up: "The Son of Man's gon' suffer, be rejected by the elders and top priests, get killed, and rise after three days."
8.32: He said it plain. But Peter pulled Him aside and started rebuking Him.
8.33: Jesus turned around, looked at the disciples, and said to Peter, "Get behind Me, Satan. You ain't focused on God's business—just human stuff."
8.34: Then He called everybody together, not just the Twelve. "If you wanna follow Me, deny yourself, pick up your cross, and let's go.
8.35: If you tryna save your own life, you gon' lose it. But if you lose your life for Me and this message? You gon' find it.
8.36: What good is it to win the whole world but lose your soul?
8.37: What could you trade for your soul anyway?
8.38: If you ashamed of Me and My words in this fake and sinful generation, the Son of Man gon' be ashamed of you when He show up in His Father's glory with the holy angels."

9.1: Jesus said, "Let Me tell y'all something real: some of y'all right here ain't gon' die 'til you see the Kingdom show up in full power."
9.2: Six days later, Jesus took Peter, James, and John up on a high mountain. Just them. Then boom—He changed right in front of their eyes.
9.3: His clothes started shinin' bright, whiter than any bleach could ever get 'em.
9.4: Outta nowhere, Elijah and Moses popped up, choppin' it up with Jesus.
9.5: Peter, nervous and not really knowing what to say, was like, "Rabbi, it's good we here. Let's build three shelters—one for You, one for Moses, one for Elijah."
9.6: He was shook, talkin' off nerves.
9.7: Then a cloud pulled up, and a voice came out it: "This right here is My Son, who I love. Y'all better listen to Him!"
9.8: And just like that, Moses and Elijah vanished. Only Jesus was left with them.
9.9: On the way down the mountain, Jesus told them, "Don't tell nobody what y'all saw until the Son of Man rises from the dead."
9.10: They kept quiet but kept wonderin', "What He mean 'rise from the dead'?"
9.11: Then they asked, "Why the teachers say Elijah gotta come first?"
9.12: Jesus said, "Yeah, Elijah comes first to fix things. But why y'all think it's written that the Son of Man gotta suffer and get rejected?
9.13: Elijah already came. And they did him dirty, just like the scriptures said."
9.14: When they came back down, a big crowd had formed, and some scribes were arguin' with the other disciples.
9.15: Soon as folks saw Jesus, they were amazed and ran over.
9.16: Jesus was like, "What y'all talkin' about?"
9.17: A man spoke up: "Teacher, I brought my son—he got a mute spirit.
9.18: It throws him down, makes him foam at the mouth, grind his teeth, lock up. I asked Your disciples to help, but they couldn't."
9.19: Jesus sighed, "Man, this faithless generation… how long I gotta deal with y'all? Bring him here."
9.20: They brought the boy. As soon as the spirit saw Jesus, it threw the boy into a fit—he hit the ground rollin', foamin' up.
9.21: Jesus asked his dad, "How long this been goin' on?" He said, "Since he was a kid.
9.22: Sometimes the spirit try to kill him—throwin' him in fire or water. But if You can do anything, please help us."
9.23: Jesus said, "If I can? Everything's possible if you believe."
9.24: The father cried out, "I believe! But help me where I still got doubts!"
9.25: Jesus saw the crowd growing, so He rebuked the spirit: "You deaf and mute demon, I command you, come out and don't come back!"
9.26: The spirit screamed, convulsed the boy hard, then left. The boy looked dead—folks thought he was gone.
9.27: But Jesus grabbed his hand, lifted him up, and he stood up whole.
9.28: Later on, the disciples asked Jesus privately, "Why couldn't we cast it out?"
9.29: He said, "This one only comes out by prayer and fasting."
9.30: They left and passed through Galilee, but Jesus kept it lowkey.
9.31: He told His disciples, "The Son of Man gon' be betrayed, killed, and rise after three days."
9.32: They didn't get it… and were too scared to ask.
9.33: In Capernaum, Jesus asked, "What was y'all arguin' about on the road?"
9.34: They stayed quiet—'cause they'd been debating who was the GOAT among them.
9.35: Jesus sat down like a real teacher and said, "If you wanna be first, be last. Be a servant to everybody."
9.36: Then He grabbed a little kid, put him in front of them, and said,
9.37: "Whoever welcomes a child like this in My name welcomes Me—and not just Me, but the One who sent Me."
9.38: John said, "Teacher, we saw someone casting out demons in Your name. We tried to shut him down 'cause he ain't one of us."
9.39: Jesus said, "Don't do that. If he using My name to do good, he ain't gon' turn and speak evil of Me.
9.40: If they ain't against us, they with us.
9.41: Anybody who give y'all a drink just because you belong to Me? They ain't gon' lose their reward."
9.42: "But if you cause one of these little believers to stumble? It'd be better for you to get tossed in the sea with a millstone chained to your neck."
9.43: "If your hand makes you sin, cut it off. Better to go to Heaven with one hand than to end up in hell with two.
9.44: Where the fire never quits and the worms don't die.
9.45: Same with your foot. If it makes you stumble, cut it off.
9.46: Where the fire never quits and the worms don't die.
9.47: If your eye keeps dragging you into sin, pluck it out. Better to step into God's Kingdom with one eye than land in hellfire with both.
9.48: That place where the worms don't die and the flames don't quit."
9.49: "Everybody gon' get seasoned with fire—some refinement, some testing.
9.50: Salt is good, but if you lose your flavor, how you gon' get it back? Be seasoned—stay salty in a righteous way. And live in peace with each other."

10.1: Jesus left that spot and went down to Judea, across the Jordan. Folks crowded around again, and like always, He started teachin' them.
10.2: Then here come the Pharisees tryna trap Him, askin', "Is it cool for a man to divorce his wife?"
10.3: Jesus hit back, "What did Moses say?"
10.4: They said, "Moses said we could write divorce papers and send her away."
10.5: Jesus was like, "Yeah, but that was 'cause y'all hearts hard. That ain't how God wanted it from the jump.
10.6: Since creation, God made 'em male and female.
10.7: That's why a man leaves his momma and daddy and gets locked in with his wife,
10.8: And the two become one body. Not two no more, but one.
10.9: So what God put together, don't let nobody tear apart."
10.10: Later, the disciples brought it back up at the house.
10.11: Jesus said, "If a man divorces his wife and marries somebody else, he cheatin' on her.
10.12: Same thing for a woman divorcing her man and gettin' remarried—it's adultery."
10.13: People started bringin' kids to Jesus so He could bless them, but the disciples tried to shut it down.
10.14: Jesus wasn't havin' it. He got tight and said, "Let these babies come to Me! Don't stop 'em. The Kingdom belongs to folks who come like this.
10.15: If you don't receive the Kingdom like a lil child, you ain't gettin' in."
10.16: Then He picked them kids up, laid hands on 'em, and blessed them.
10.17: As Jesus was leavin', this man came runnin', dropped to his knees and asked, "Good Teacher, what I gotta do to get eternal life?"
10.18: Jesus said, "Why you callin' Me good? Ain't nobody good but God.
10.19: You know the rules—don't cheat, don't kill, don't steal, don't lie, don't scam, respect your parents."
10.20: The man said, "Been doin' that since I was a kid."
10.21: Jesus looked at him with love and said, "One thing missing—go sell all your stuff, give the money to the poor, then come follow Me. You'll have treasure in heaven."
10.22: The man's whole mood dropped. He left sad, 'cause he had a lot of stuff.
10.23: Jesus looked around and said, "It's hard for rich folks to enter the Kingdom."
10.24: The disciples were shook. Jesus said again, "It's hard for folks who trust money to make it into God's Kingdom.
10.25: It's easier for a camel to squeeze through a needle's eye than a rich man to enter."
10.26: They were really shook now: "Then who can anybody be saved?"
10.27: Jesus said, "With people? It ain't happenin'. But with God? Everything possible."
10.28: Peter jumped in: "We gave up everything to follow You!"
10.29: Jesus said, "Anybody who gave up home, family, land for Me and the gospel gon' get way more—not just later, but now too. It'll come with struggle though.
10.30: And eternal life in the next one.
10.31: But don't get it twisted—some folks who look first now? Gon' be last later. And some last now? Gon' be first."
10.32: On the road to Jerusalem, Jesus was walkin' ahead. The disciples were amazed, but lowkey scared.
10.33: He pulled them aside and said, "We goin' up to Jerusalem. The Son of Man gon' get betrayed, sentenced to death, handed over to outsiders.
10.34: They gon' clown Him, spit on Him, beat Him, and kill Him. But three days later? He gettin' up."
10.35: Then James and John came bold, like, "Jesus, do us a favor."
10.37: They said, "Let us sit next to You in glory—one on the right, one on the left."
10.38: Jesus said, "Y'all don't even know what you askin'. Can you drink the cup I'ma drink? Can you handle the baptism I'ma go through?"
10.40: Jesus said, "Okay, y'all will go through some stuff like Me. But where folks sit? That ain't mine to give. That's already been set."
10.41: When the other ten heard what James and John were askin'? Oh they were heated.
10.42: Jesus pulled 'em all in and said, "Look, the world loves to flex power. But y'all? That's not how it's gon' be.
10.43: If you wanna be great, serve.
10.44: If you wanna be first, be everybody's servant.
10.45: Even I ain't come to be served, but to serve—and to give My life to set people free."
10.46: They rolled into Jericho. As they headed out, a big crowd followed. Bartimaeus, a blind man, was beggin' by the road.
10.47: When he heard Jesus was near, he started shoutin', "Jesus! Son of David! Have mercy on me!"
10.48: Folks tried to shut him up, but he got louder: "SON OF DAVID, HAVE MERCY ON ME!"
10.50: So they told Bartimaeus, "Cheer up! He callin' you."
10.51: He threw off his cloak, jumped up, and ran to Jesus.
10.52: Jesus asked, "What you want Me to do for you?"
10.53: Bartimaeus said, "Rabbi, I wanna see again."
10.54: Jesus said, "Go ahead—your faith made you well."
10.55: Right then and there, Bartimaeus got his sight… and followed Jesus down the road.

11.1: When they got close to Jerusalem, near Bethphage and Bethany by the Mount of Olives, Jesus sent out two of His disciples.
11.2: He told them, "Go to the village across from here. As soon as you walk in, you gon' see a young donkey tied up that ain't nobody ever rode. Untie it and bring it back.
11.3: And if somebody asks you, 'Why y'all takin' that?' just say, 'The Lord need it,' and they'll let it go."
11.4: So they dipped and found the colt tied up outside on the street, just like Jesus said. They started untyin' it.
11.5: Some folks standing nearby said, "What y'all doin' with that colt?"
11.6: They said exactly what Jesus told 'em to say—and the folks let them go.
11.7: They brought the colt back to Jesus, threw their coats on it, and Jesus sat on it.
11.8: A bunch of people laid their coats down on the road. Others were cuttin' palm branches off trees and laying them down too.
11.9: And the crowd—front and back—started shoutin': "Hosanna! Blessed is the One who comes in the name of the Lord!
11.10: Blessed is the kingdom of our father David, Comin' through in the name of the Lord! Hosanna in the highest!"
11.11: Jesus rolled into Jerusalem and walked up in the temple. He looked around at everything, but since it was late, He dipped back out to Bethany with the twelve.
11.12: The next day, they leavin' Bethany and Jesus got hungry.
11.13: He saw a fig tree from a distance with leaves and thought maybe it had somethin'. But when He got there, it was just leaves—wasn't even fig season.
11.14: Jesus said to the tree, "Ain't nobody eatin' from you ever again." His disciples heard it.
11.15: When they got to Jerusalem, Jesus went into the temple and started wildin'—He flipped tables, kicked out the folks buyin' and sellin', and knocked over the dove-sellers' booths.
11.16: He wouldn't even let folks walk through the temple carryin' stuff.
11.17: Then He said, "Ain't it written, 'My house gon' be a house of prayer for all people'? But y'all turned it into a den of thieves."
11.18: The religious leaders heard about it and started plotting to kill Him. They were scared 'cause the people were blown away by how He taught.
11.19: That evening, Jesus left the city.
11.20: The next morning, they passed by that same fig tree, and it was dried up from the roots.
11.21: Peter remembered and said, "Rabbi, look! That fig tree you cursed is dead!"
11.23: I'm tellin' y'all the truth—if you say to this mountain, 'Move and throw yourself in the sea,' and don't doubt but believe it's gon' happen—it will happen.
11.24: That's why I say, when you pray and ask for somethin', believe like it's already yours—and it'll be yours.
11.25: But when you pray, if you holdin' something against somebody, forgive them, so your Father in heaven can forgive you.
11.26: But if you don't forgive, your Father ain't forgivin' you either."
11.27: They came back to Jerusalem. As Jesus was walkin' in the temple, the chief priests, scribes, and elders rolled up on Him.
11.28: They asked, "Who gave You the right to do all this? Who said You could?"
11.29: Jesus said, "I'ma ask y'all one thing, and if y'all answer Me, I'll tell you where my authority come from.
11.30: John's baptism—was that from heaven or just from man? Tell Me that."
11.31: They huddled up like, "If we say 'heaven,' He gon' ask why we ain't believe John.
11.32: But if we say 'man,' these folks gon' turn on us 'cause they all think John was a real prophet."
11.33: So they played it safe and said, "We don't know." And Jesus said, "Then I ain't tellin' y'all either."

12.1: Jesus started speakin' to them using stories. He said, "A man planted a vineyard, put a fence around it, dug out a place for the wine to drip, built a lookout tower, then rented it out to some workers and dipped out to another country.
12.2: When it was time to harvest, he sent a servant to collect his share of the fruit.
12.3: But the workers grabbed that man, beat him down, and sent him back empty-handed.
12.4: Then he sent another servant. This time, they threw rocks at him, hit him in the head, and treated him like trash.
12.5: The man sent another one, and they straight-up killed him. He kept sendin' more—some got beat down, some got killed.
12.6: Now the man had one left—his son, who he loved dearly. He figured they'd respect his son, so he sent him last.
12.7: But those workers said to each other, 'That's the heir! Let's kill him, and the vineyard gon' be ours.'
12.8: So they grabbed him, killed him, and threw his body out the vineyard.
12.9: "So what y'all think the owner gon' do? He gon' pull up, destroy them wicked workers, and lease the vineyard to somebody else.
12.10: Ain't y'all read this before? 'The stone the builders threw away Done became the cornerstone.
12.11: The Lord did that, And it's wild to see.'"
12.12: They wanted to snatch Jesus up right there, 'cause they knew He was talkin' about them. But they was scared of the crowd, so they dipped off instead.
12.13: Then they sent some Pharisees and Herod's folks to Jesus, tryna trap Him in His words.
12.14: They came up and said, "Teacher, we know You real and don't care about nobody's status. You speak the truth straight from God. So tell us—should we pay taxes to Caesar or not?"
12.15: Jesus peeped their game and said, "Why y'all testin' Me? Bring Me a coin so I can see it."
12.16: They handed Him one. He asked, "Whose face and name on here?" They said, "Caesar's."
12.17: Jesus said, "Then give Caesar what belongs to Caesar—and give God what belongs to God." They ain't know what to say after that.
12.18: Then the Sadducees—who don't believe in resurrection—stepped up and asked Jesus a question.
12.19: "Teacher," they said, "Moses told us if a man dies without kids, his brother gotta marry the widow and give her children in his name.
12.20: Now, there were seven brothers. First one got married, died, no kids.
12.21: Second brother married her, died too, still no kids. Same with the third.
12.22: All seven brothers had her and died without children. Then the woman died too.
12.23: So when everybody comes back to life, whose wife she gon' be? All seven had her."
12.24: Jesus said, "Y'all wrong, and it's 'cause y'all don't know the Scriptures or God's power.
12.25: When folks rise from the dead, they don't get married—they gon' be like angels in heaven.
12.26: And about the dead rising—didn't you read what Moses wrote about the burning bush? God said, 'I'm the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.'
12.27: He ain't the God of the dead—He's God of the living. Y'all real wrong on this one."
12.28: One of the scribes overheard the convo and saw Jesus had great answers. He asked, "Which commandment is the most important of all?"
12.29: Jesus said, "The first one is: 'Hear, O Israel, the Lord our God is one.
12.30: Love the Lord your God with all your heart, all your soul, all your mind, and all your strength.'
12.31: And the second one right behind it is: 'Love your neighbor like you love yourself.' Ain't no commandments greater than these."
12.32: The scribe said, "Facts, Teacher. You spoke real. There's one God, no other.
12.33: Lovin' Him with everything you got—and lovin' your neighbor—that's better than any burnt offering or sacrifice."
12.34: Jesus saw the man had real wisdom and told him, "You not far from God's Kingdom." After that, nobody had the nerve to ask Him nothin' else.
12.35: While teachin' in the temple, Jesus said, "How y'all say the Christ is David's son?
12.36: 'Cause David himself, speakin' by the Spirit, said: 'The Lord said to my Lord, Sit at My right hand Till I put Your enemies under Your feet.'
12.37: If David calls Him 'Lord,' how is He his son?" The crowd was lovin' what Jesus said.
12.38: Jesus kept teachin', "Watch out for them scribes who like to strut around in long robes, lovin' the attention in the streets.
12.39: They want the best seats in the synagogue and the top spots at dinner.
12.40: They be robbin' widows and actin' holy with them long prayers. Trust, they gon' be judged harder."
12.41: Jesus sat across from the temple offering box and watched folks droppin' in their money. The rich were droppin' big stacks.
12.42: But this one poor widow came up and dropped in two little coins—barely anything.
12.43: Jesus called His disciples and said, "Let me tell y'all the truth: That poor woman gave more than everybody else.
12.44: They gave outta their overflow. But she gave everything she had—even the little she was livin' on."

13.1: As Jesus was leavin' the temple, one of His disciples said, "Teacher, look at these big ol' stones and buildings!"
13.2: Jesus said, "You see all this? Ain't a single stone gon' be left sittin' on another. All of it gettin' torn down."
13.3: Later on, while Jesus was chillin' on the Mount of Olives across from the temple, Peter, James, John, and Andrew pulled Him to the side and asked,
13.4: "Tell us, when's all this gon' happen? What signs should we be watchin' for?"
13.5: Jesus started in: "Y'all better watch out and don't let nobody play y'all.
13.6: A lotta folks gon' come in My name talkin' 'I'm Him!' and foolin' folks left and right.
13.7: You gon' hear 'bout wars poppin' off and whispers of more war. Don't panic. That stuff gotta happen, but that ain't the end yet.
13.8: Whole nations gon' beef with each other. Kingdoms too. Earthquakes gon' hit different places, famines gon' pop up. But that's just the beginning—just the labor pains.
13.9: Look, be on guard. They gon' hand y'all over to courts, beat y'all in church, and drag y'all in front of kings 'cause of Me. Y'all gon' be witnesses in front of 'em.
13.10: But first, this gospel gotta be preached everywhere, all across the nations.
13.11: When they snatch y'all up and hand y'all over, don't stress about what to say. Just say whatever the Spirit gives you in that moment—it ain't you talkin', it's the Holy Ghost.
13.12: Folks gon' be turnin' on each other—brother against brother, daddy against child. Kids gon' snitch on parents, get 'em killed.
13.13: Everybody gon' hate y'all 'cause of Me. But whoever sticks it out to the end? They the ones gon' be saved."
13.14: "Now when y'all see that wild mess Daniel talked about—the 'abomination of desolation'—standin' where it don't belong (yeah, reader, I'm talkin' to you), run for the hills if you in Judea.
13.15: If you up on the roof, don't even go inside to grab nothin'.
13.16: If you out in the field, don't run back for your coat.
13.17: Prayers up for pregnant women and moms with babies—it's gon' be hard for them.
13.18: Pray it don't go down in the winter.
13.19: 'Cause those days gon' be hell—worse than anything that's ever happened since God made the world.
13.20: If God ain't cut those days short, nobody would make it. But for the sake of His chosen ones, He shortened it."
13.21: "If somebody tell y'all, 'Hey, Christ over here!' or 'He right there!'—don't believe 'em.
13.22: Fake messiahs and false prophets gon' pop up doin' wild signs and wonders, tryin' to trick even God's chosen, if they could.
13.23: So stay alert! I already told y'all what's comin'."
13.24: "But after all that tribulation, the sun gon' go dark, the moon won't shine,
13.25: the stars gon' fall, and even the powers in heaven gon' shake.
13.26: Then they gon' see the Son of Man comin' through the clouds, flexin' with power and glory.
13.27: He gon' send out angels to round up His chosen from everywhere—from the far ends of earth to the highest place in heaven."
13.28: "Now check this parable out—when a fig tree starts gettin' soft branches and sproutin' leaves, you already know summer almost here.
13.29: Same thing here: when y'all see these signs goin' down, know it's right around the corner.
13.30: I'm tellin' y'all for real—this generation won't pass before all this happens.
13.31: Heaven and earth might fade out, but My words? They stay forever."
13.32: "But when it's all gon' pop off? Nobody knows that day or hour—not the angels, not even the Son—only the Father know.
13.33: So stay woke, watch, and pray. You don't know when it's goin' down.
13.34: It's like a man leavin' the crib and puttin' his folks in charge, each one with a job, and the door guy on lookout.
13.35: So stay ready—you don't know if the boss comin' at night, at midnight, when the rooster crows, or early morning.
13.36: You don't wanna get caught sleepin' when He shows up outta nowhere.
13.37: What I'm tellin' y'all, I'm tellin' everybody: Watch!"

14.1: Two days before Passover and the Feast of Unleavened Bread, the chief priests and scribes was plottin' on how they could catch Jesus slippin' and kill Him on the low.
14.2: But they was like, "Not during the feast tho, or folks might wild out and start a riot."
14.3: Jesus was chillin' in Bethany at Simon the leper's spot, sittin' at the table, when this woman came through with a fancy alabaster jar full of expensive spikenard oil. She cracked it open and poured it all over His head.
14.4: Some folks at the table got mad and started whisperin', "Why she wastin' that good-smellin' oil like that?"
14.5: "She coulda sold that for over 300 coins and gave the money to the poor." And they started scoldin' her hard.
14.6: But Jesus shut it down like, "Leave her alone. Why y'all stressin' her? She just did somethin' real beautiful for Me."
14.7: "Poor folks gon' always be around, and y'all can help 'em whenever. But I ain't gon' be here like that forever."
14.8: "She did what she could—anointed My body early, gettin' Me ready for burial."
14.9: "I'ma tell y'all the truth—wherever this gospel gets preached around the world, folks gon' talk about what she did. That's her legacy."
14.10: Then Judas Iscariot—one of Jesus' own crew—went to the chief priests to sell Him out.
14.11: When they heard that, they got hype and promised to pay him. From then on, Judas was lookin' for the right time to hand Jesus over.
14.12: On the first day of Unleavened Bread, when they was sacrificin' the Passover lamb, the disciples asked Jesus, "Where You want us to go and set things up so You can eat the Passover meal?"
14.13: Jesus sent two of them out and said, "Go into the city, and you'll meet a man carryin' a water jug. Follow him."
14.14: "When he go in the house, say to the owner, 'The Teacher said, where the guest room at for Me and My crew to eat the Passover?'"
14.15: "He gon' show y'all a big upstairs room, already set. That's the spot. Get it ready."
14.16: The disciples dipped out, went to the city, and found everything just like Jesus said. So they prepped the Passover meal.
14.17: That evening, Jesus came through with the Twelve.
14.18: While they was sittin' down eatin', Jesus said, "For real, one of y'all sittin' at this table with Me is gon' betray Me."
14.19: They all got shook and sad, and started askin' one by one, "It ain't me, is it?"
14.20: Jesus said, "It's one of the Twelve—one of y'all dippin' bread in the same dish as Me."
14.21: "The Son of Man gon' go just like it was written, but woe to the one who sells Him out. It woulda been better if he ain't even been born."
14.22: While they was eatin', Jesus grabbed some bread, blessed it, broke it, and gave it to them. He said, "Take it. This My body."
14.23: Then He took the cup, gave thanks, passed it around, and they all drank.
14.24: He said, "This My blood—the new covenant—poured out for many."
14.25: "I'ma tell y'all straight—I ain't drinkin' no more wine until I drink it fresh in God's Kingdom."
14.26: After they sang a hymn, they rolled out to the Mount of Olives.
14.27: Jesus told 'em, "Tonight, all y'all gon' fall back 'cause of Me. The Scriptures say, 'I'ma strike the Shepherd, and the sheep gon' scatter.'"
14.28: "But after I rise up, I'll be in Galilee waitin' on y'all."
14.29: Peter said, "Even if everybody else fall off, I ain't goin' nowhere."
14.30: Jesus replied, "Truth is, tonight—before the rooster crows twice—you gon' deny Me three times."
14.31: Peter got loud with it, "Even if I gotta die with You, I won't deny You!" And all the others was sayin' the same thing.
14.32: They pulled up to a place called Gethsemane. Jesus told the rest, "Y'all sit here while I go pray."
14.33: He took Peter, James, and John with Him, and He started feelin' real heavy and troubled.
14.34: He said, "My soul is crushed, y'all… like I'm dyin' inside. Stay here and keep watch."
14.35: He walked a little farther, fell on the ground, and started prayin' that maybe the moment could pass Him by.
14.36: He said, "Abba, Father, You can do anything. Please take this cup from Me. But still—not My will, but Yours."
14.37: Then Jesus came back and caught them sleepin'. He said to Peter, "Simon, you sleepin'? You couldn't stay woke for one hour?"
14.38: "Watch and pray, so you don't fall into temptation. The spirit be down, but the flesh? Weak."
14.39: He left again and prayed, sayin' the same thing.
14.40: When He came back, they was knocked out again—their eyes was heavy. They ain't even know what to say to Him.
14.41: Third time He came back, He said, "Y'all still sleepin' and layin' up? That's enough. Time's up. The Son of Man 'bout to be handed over to some sinners."
14.42: "Get up, let's go. My betrayer right here."
14.43: Right while He was still talkin', Judas—one of the Twelve—rolled up with a whole mob. They had swords and clubs, sent by the chief priests, scribes, and elders.
14.44: Judas had told them ahead of time, "The one I kiss—that's Him. Grab Him and make sure He don't get away."
14.45: He walked up on Jesus, said, "Rabbi! Rabbi!" and kissed Him.
14.46: Then they grabbed Jesus and arrested Him.
14.47: But one of the people standin' there pulled out a sword, swung on the high priest's servant, and sliced off his ear.
14.48: Jesus said, "Y'all really came at Me like I'm some kind of criminal? Swords and clubs and all that?"
14.49: "I was at the temple every day teachin', and y'all ain't touch Me. But all this gotta go down so the Scriptures can come true."
14.50: Then everybody dipped. Left Him by Himself.
14.51: There was a young man followin' Jesus, wearin' nothin' but a linen sheet around his body. When they tried to grab him—
14.52: He slipped out the cloth and ran off naked.
14.53: They took Jesus to the high priest, where all the chief priests, elders, and scribes was already gathered up.
14.54: Peter followed Him from a distance, all the way into the high priest's courtyard. He sat with the servants, warm by the fire.
14.55: The chief priests and whole council was lookin' for something to use against Jesus so they could get Him killed—but they couldn't find nothin'.
14.56: A bunch of folks lied on Him, but their stories ain't match.
14.57: Then some stood up and lied again, sayin',
14.58: "We heard Him say, 'I'll tear down this temple made by hands and in three days build another one not made by hands.'"
14.59: But even then, they couldn't get their lies to line up.
14.60: The high priest stood up in the middle and said, "You not gon' say nothin'? You hear what these folks sayin' about You?"
14.61: But Jesus ain't say a word. He stayed quiet. So the high priest asked again, "Are You the Messiah? The Son of the Blessed One?"
14.62: Jesus said, "I am. And you gon' see the Son of Man sittin' at the right hand of Power, comin' with the clouds of heaven."
14.63: Then the high priest ripped his clothes and said, "We don't need no more witnesses!"
14.64: "Y'all heard that blasphemy. What y'all think?" And they all said, "He deserves to die."
14.65: Then they started spittin' on Him, blindfolded Him, hit Him, and said, "Prophesy!" Even the officers was slappin' Him around.
14.66: Meanwhile, Peter was down in the courtyard. One of the high priest's servant girls came by.
14.67: She saw Peter warm by the fire, looked at him hard, and said, "You was with Jesus of Nazareth too."
14.68: But he denied it: "I don't even know what you talkin' about." Then he stepped out on the porch—and the rooster crowed.
14.69: The same servant girl saw him again and told the folks standin' there, "He one of them."
14.70: He denied it again. Then a little later, the people nearby said to Peter, "You gotta be one of them. You a Galilean—your accent givin' it away."
14.71: Peter started cussin' and swearin', "I don't know this Man y'all talkin' about!"
14.72: The rooster crowed a second time. Then Peter remembered what Jesus told him: "Before the rooster crows twice, you gon' deny Me three times." And when he realized it, he broke down and cried.

15.1: Early in the mornin', the chief priests linked up with the elders, scribes, and the whole council. They tied Jesus up, took Him to Pilate, and handed Him over.
15.2: Pilate asked Him, "You the King of the Jews?" Jesus said, "You said it."
15.3: The chief priests started throwin' all kinds of accusations at Him.
15.4: Pilate asked Him again, "You not gon' say nothin'? You hear all this they sayin' about You?"
15.5: But Jesus ain't say a word, and that had Pilate shook.
15.6: During the festival, Pilate had a tradition—he'd let one prisoner go, whoever the people picked.
15.7: One of the locked-up folks was Barabbas. He was in there with some rebels who caught a body during a riot.
15.8: The crowd pulled up and asked Pilate to do what he usually did.
15.9: Pilate said, "Y'all want me to let go the King of the Jews?"
15.10: He knew the priests was only pushin' for Jesus' death 'cause they was jealous.
15.11: But the chief priests hyped up the crowd to ask for Barabbas instead.
15.12: Pilate asked again, "So what y'all want me to do with this one y'all call King of the Jews?"
15.14: Pilate said, "Why? What He do wrong?" But they just yelled louder, "Crucify Him!"
15.15: So Pilate, tryna keep the people happy, let Barabbas go. Then he had Jesus beaten and handed Him over to be crucified.
15.16: The soldiers took Jesus into the palace, called the Praetorium, and brought the whole squad together.
15.17: They dressed Him in purple and twisted a crown of thorns, put it on His head.
15.18: They started mockin' Him, sayin', "Hail, King of the Jews!"
15.19: They beat Him on the head with a stick, spit on Him, and fake-worshiped Him, kneelin' down like they was jokin'.
15.20: After all that, they took off the purple robe, put His clothes back on, and dragged Him off to be crucified.
15.21: They made a man named Simon from Cyrene—daddy to Alexander and Rufus—carry Jesus' cross. He was just passin' through from outta town.
15.22: They brought Jesus to a place called Golgotha—means "Place of the Skull."
15.23: They tried to give Him wine mixed with myrrh, but He ain't drink it.
15.24: They nailed Him to the cross and started gamblin' for His clothes to see who'd get what.
15.25: It was the third hour when they crucified Him.
15.26: They put a sign above Him sayin': "THE KING OF THE JEWS."
15.27: They crucified two criminals with Him—one on His right, one on His left.
15.28: So Scripture got fulfilled that said, "He was counted with the lawbreakers."
15.29: Folks walkin' by started talkin' trash, shakin' their heads like, "Ha! You the one who said You'd tear down the temple and rebuild it in three days?"
15.30: "Save Yourself and come down off that cross!"
15.31: The chief priests and scribes joined in the roast: "He saved other folks, but He can't save Himself!"
15.32: "If He really the Christ, the King of Israel, let Him come down from the cross right now. Then we'll believe Him." Even the two dudes on the crosses next to Him was throwin' shade.
15.33: Around noon, darkness covered the whole land until about 3 p.m.
15.34: At 3, Jesus shouted loud, "Eloi, Eloi, lama sabachthani?"—means "My God, My God, why You leave Me hangin'?"
15.35: Some folks nearby was like, "He callin' Elijah!"
15.36: Somebody ran, grabbed a sponge soaked in sour wine, stuck it on a stick, and gave it to Him to sip. They said, "Hold up—let's see if Elijah gon' come save Him."
15.37: Then Jesus cried out one last time and took His last breath.
15.38: The temple curtain tore clean down the middle—from top to bottom.
15.39: The Roman soldier standin' there saw how Jesus died and said, "Man… this really was the Son of God."
15.40: Some women was watchin' from a distance. Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James the Less and Joses, and Salome was there.
15.41: They used to follow Jesus and serve Him when He was in Galilee. A lotta other women came with Him to Jerusalem too.
15.42: That evening, since it was Preparation Day—the day before Sabbath—
15.43: Joseph from Arimathea, a respected council member who was waitin' for God's Kingdom, pulled up with courage and asked Pilate for Jesus' body.
15.44: Pilate was surprised Jesus was already dead. He asked the soldier if that was true.
15.45: Once the centurion confirmed it, Pilate gave Joseph the body.
15.46: Joseph bought some fine linen, took Jesus down, wrapped Him up, and laid Him in a tomb cut outta rock. Then he rolled a big stone in front of the entrance.
15.47: Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of Joses was watchin' where He got laid.

16.1: After the Sabbath was over, Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James, and Salome went and bought some spices so they could go anoint Jesus' body.
16.2: Early in the mornin' on the first day of the week, right after sunrise, they pulled up to the tomb.
16.3: On the way there, they was askin' each other, "Who gon' roll that big ol' stone out the way for us?"
16.4: But when they looked up, they saw the stone was already moved—it was huge, too.
16.5: They stepped inside the tomb and saw a young man in a long white robe sittin' on the right side. They got shook.
16.6: But he said, "Don't be scared. Y'all lookin' for Jesus from Nazareth—the One they crucified. He ain't here. He got up! Look where they laid Him."
16.7: "Now go on and tell His disciples—and make sure you tell Peter too—that He's headed to Galilee. Y'all gon' see Him there, just like He told y'all."
16.8: They ran out the tomb, tremblin' and shook. They ain't say nothin' to nobody 'cause they was scared.
16.9: Early on that first day of the week, Jesus showed Himself first to Mary Magdalene—the same one He cast seven demons outta.
16.10: She ran and told His people—the ones still grievin' and cryin'.
16.11: But when they heard He was alive and that she saw Him, they ain't believe her.
16.12: After that, He popped up in a different form to two more of them while they was walkin' out in the countryside.
16.13: They went and told the rest, but the others ain't believe them either.
16.14: Later, Jesus appeared to the Eleven while they was eatin'. He checked 'em for not believin' and for bein' hard-headed about the folks who already told 'em He rose up.
16.15: Then He said, "Go everywhere—around the whole world—and preach this good news to everybody."
16.16: "Whoever believes and gets baptized? They saved. But the ones who don't believe? Condemned."
16.17: "And this how My believers gon' roll: In My name, they gon' cast out demons. They gon' speak new tongues."
16.18: "They gon' handle snakes, drink somethin' deadly and not be hurt. They gon' lay hands on the sick and folks gon' get healed."
16.19: After Jesus finished speakin' to them, He went up to heaven and sat down at God's right hand.
16.20: And they went out preachin' everywhere. The Lord was workin' right beside them, showin' proof of the message with all kinds of signs. Amen.
